newsitem.title: RUSSIA: NATO chief leaves Russia after talks - Interfax.
newsitem.headline: NATO chief leaves Russia after talks - Interfax.

text.p: NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana left Moscow on Monday after five hours of talks with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, Interfax news agency said.
It said no details of the meeting had been released.

Solana came to Moscow to try to ease Russian fears over the Western alliance's plans to admit new members from eastern and central Europe and to start talks on forging a special relationship with Russia.

Interfax quoted sources at the Russian foreign ministry as saying the talks had ended without any statement being released, but did not rule out the possibility that a communique might be distributed later on Monday.

Moscow says NATO enlargement would threaten Russia's security and create new divisions in Europe. NATO officials said Monday's talks were intended to reassure Moscow that enlargement would not be a threat.
